text:
# Simulation output


## Overview
This family generates volume data by solving physical equations (fluid dynamics, thermodynamics, or particle transport) rather than scanning physical objects or defining static mathematical fields [G]. It solves the problem of creating temporally coherent, physically plausible volume attributes (density, temperature, velocity) for rendering [G]. It differs from [Voxelization](12-voxelization.md) by deriving data from dynamic simulation rather than geometric sampling, and from [Procedural and implicit volumes](13-procedural-and-implicit-volumes.md) by relying on time-evolving state variables rather than static spatial functions [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on the [Shared principles](11-producing-volume-data.md) of the parent family [G].

## Subtopics

### [Position Based Fluids](1765-position-based-fluids.md)
A Lagrangian particle-based fluid simulation method that enforces incompressibility by directly correcting particle positions to satisfy density constraints. It differs from pressure-based solvers by using constraint projection within a Position-Based Dynamics framework, which stabilizes the simulation and avoids density drift. It builds on [Simulation output](15-simulation-output.md) and is distinct from [Gaussian Splashing](1387-gaussian-splashing.md) and [Smoke Advection](4639-smoke-advection.md) by decoupling simulation from rendering and operating entirely in particle space. Choose this when real-time, incompressible fluid behavior is required without the stability issues of pressure-based solvers [G].

### [Voxel-based 3D Fire Simulation](3411-voxel-based-3d-fire-simulation.md)
Simulates fire dynamics by storing velocity, smoke density, temperature, and fuel level attributes in a discrete 3D voxel grid. It solves the Navier-Stokes equations to propagate fluid motion, augmented by specific buoyancy and vorticity forces to model the rising, curling behavior of fire. It is distinguished from particle-based methods by its structured grid storage, which allows for efficient divergence and advection calculations using 3D textures. Choose this when visual fidelity of fire dynamics (ignition, burning, extinction) is needed [G].

### [Smoke Advection](4639-smoke-advection.md)
Transports scalar quantities, such as density and temperature, through a fluid velocity field to visualize smoke effects in real-time simulations. It distinguishes itself from pure velocity advection by introducing source terms (e.g., Gaussian splats) and coupling scalar fields (like temperature) back into the dynamics via buoyant forces, rather than treating them as passive tracers alone. Choose this when smoke appearance and thermal effects are critical [G].

### [Gaussian Splashing](1387-gaussian-splashing.md)
A method that performs physical simulations using [Position-Based Fluids](#1765-position-based-fluids.md). It differs from standard PBF by integrating the simulation directly into a [3D Gaussian Splatting rendering pipeline](#3415-gaussian-splatting-rendering-pipeline.md), allowing for physically accurate rendering of fluid surfaces without traditional mesh extraction. Choose this when using 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) for real-time fluid rendering and surface reconstruction is desired [G].

### [GPU-based Fluid Simulation with Voxel Rendering](7400-gpu-based-fluid-simulation-with-voxel-rendering.md)
Integrates real-time incompressible fluid simulation with [sparse voxel-based rasterization](#3032-sparse-voxel-rasterization.md) on graphics hardware, specifically using Direct3D [geometry shaders](#4369-geometry-shader-quads.md) for rendering and compute shaders for simulation. Choose this when hardware-accelerated, real-time fluid simulation with voxel rendering is required [G].

### [Niagara Fluids Volume Rendering](7739-niagara-fluids-volume-rendering.md)
Repurposes a grid-based physics simulation system for volume rendering by ignoring the simulation step ('do nothing' simulation) and using only the rendering pipeline. Choose this when leveraging a game engine's visual scripting system for volume rendering without active physics computation [G].

### Smoke Source Injection
A Unity MonoBehaviour component that injects density and velocity into the Navier-Stokes solver at the transform's world position during FixedUpdate [S1, unofficial]. It differs from global source terms by providing localized, object-driven injection of smoke [S1, unofficial]. Choose this when interactive, object-based smoke emission is required in a game engine context [S1, unofficial].

### Fire Reaction Coordinate
Tracks a reaction coordinate to simulate fire, which indicates time since ignition and fuel exhaustion [S2, unofficial]. The reaction coordinate $Y$ evolves as $\frac{\partial Y}{\partial t} = -(u \cdot \nabla) Y - k$, where $u$ is velocity and $k$ is a constant decrement per time step [S2, unofficial]. A value of 1 indicates just-ignited gas, and a value < 0 indicates fuel exhaustion [S2, unofficial]. It differs from simple density fields by explicitly modeling the fuel consumption process [S2, unofficial]. Choose this when realistic fire behavior (ignition, burning, extinction) is needed [S2, unofficial].

### Buoyant Force for Smoke
Adds a buoyant force to the velocity field based on temperature differences to make hot smoke rise and cool smoke fall [S2, unofficial]. The buoyant force is calculated as $\mathbf{f}_{buoyancy} = \frac{Pmg}{R} \left( \frac{1}{T_0} - \frac{1}{T} \right) \mathbf{z}$, where $P$ is pressure, $m$ is molar mass, $g$ is gravity, $R$ is the universal gas constant, $T_0$ is ambient temperature, $T$ is advected temperature, and $\mathbf{z}$ is the normalized upward vector [S2, unofficial]. It differs from neutral buoyancy simulations by introducing temperature-dependent vertical [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) [S2, unofficial]. Choose this when realistic smoke rise and cooling effects are required [S2, unofficial].

### Massless Particle System
Particles are used as tracer elements to visualize flow, as droplets to model fire suppression, or as fuel elements (embers) [S3, unofficial]. Positions are determined by a differential equation assuming drag force is large compared to gravity [S3, unofficial]. Particle positions are determined using $\frac{dx_p}{dt} = V(x_p, t)$, where $x_p$ is particle position and $V$ is velocity [S3, unofficial]. It differs from dense particle fluids by treating particles as passive tracers or sparse embers rather than a continuous medium [S3, unofficial]. Choose this for visualizing flow paths or sparse particulate effects like embers [S3, unofficial].

## Background
Jos Stam's stable fluids [G] laid the groundwork for Eulerian grid-based smoke simulation. The integration of fire dynamics with reaction coordinates was popularized by Nguyen et al. (2002) in the context of GPU-based fluid simulation [S2, unofficial]. Massless particle systems have been used in fire safety visualization tools like Smokeview, developed by NIST, for decades [S3, unofficial].
